note_on_method: Claims about the world (how many courts a park has, what kind they are, whether they are lit, when the gate opens) come from the City of Albuquerque's pickleball page and are cited. Claims about coverage are facts about this dataset rather than about Bernalillo County. Albuquerque is the first New Mexico city to be published, and it is the one city of this county on this page.

slots.coverage:
One city in Bernalillo County is published here: Albuquerque, with thirteen venues and eighty-six courts checked against the City's own pickleball page. Albuquerque is the first New Mexico city on this site and the first in Bernalillo County. Nothing else in the county has been read. Los Ranchos de Albuquerque has not been checked against a named source, the County's own parks have not been read, and Rio Rancho is in Sandoval County.

Three further City venues are named rather than dropped: Pat Hurley Park, Alamosa Park and Ventana Ranch Park, twenty-eight courts between them, twenty of them lit. All three are refused because neither the US Census address file nor OpenStreetMap finds the address the City writes. Two of the City's three lighting statements belong to those refused parks, which is why a city with forty-one stated lit courts publishes twenty-one.
slots.distribution:
What we cover in this county sits in one city, and inside it the courts are lopsided. Thirty-nine of the eighty-six are at the two venues the City calls its "dedicated pickleball complexes": thirty-three at Manzano Mesa Pickleball Complex in the south-east and six at Villela Pickleball Courts in the north-east. The other forty-seven are spread across eleven parks, none larger than eight. Manzano Mesa alone holds more than a third of the county's courts, and its thirty-three is the largest single-venue count on this site.

Court kind splits the set a second way. Forty-one courts are dedicated or permanent in the City's words, and forty-two are pickleball lines on tennis courts; Wells Park's three are of unstated kind. Lighting is a sharper split: twenty-one courts, all at Manzano Mesa, are stated lit, and the other sixty-five carry no lighting answer at all. Hours are stated at the two complexes, 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily, and nowhere else. The City's addresses put seven published venues in the NE, five in the NW, one in the SE and none in the SW.
slots.gaps:
This is an Albuquerque page under a county heading, and outside the City nothing has been read.

Within the City, three venues are missing because their addresses do not resolve. Pat Hurley Park's "3828 Rincon Rd NW", Alamosa Park's "1100 Bataan SW" and Ventana Ranch Park's "10000 Universe NW" are found by neither the US Census address file nor OpenStreetMap. Those three are worth twenty-eight courts, twenty of them lit, nearly half the lit courts the City states anywhere in Albuquerque.

The City's page also holds an older version of its table inside an HTML comment, invisible in a browser. It disagrees with the visible one at four venues and names three parks (Barelas, Los Altos and Zuni) the visible table does not. Nothing in it is treated as a fact here. Beyond that the silences are ordinary: no price, no surface, no indoor or outdoor, no nets, no parking, and lighting at one venue in thirteen. No club, school or private facility appears, because none publishes a source that has been read.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts are there in Bernalillo County?
faqs.a: No honest page can tell you the county total. What has been checked is 86 courts across thirteen venues, all in Albuquerque, each with a source and a date. The City names three further parks with 28 courts that cannot be published, and the County's own parks and Los Ranchos have not been read.

It is the only municipality in the county whose courts have been confirmed against a named source. Los Ranchos de Albuquerque and the County's own parks have not been read, and Rio Rancho is in Sandoval County, so it would never appear on this page.

faqs.q: What is the largest venue in the county?
faqs.a: Manzano Mesa Pickleball Complex, at 501 Elizabeth SE in Albuquerque: "33 Courts (21 Lighted)" in the City's own cell, open 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily. No other published venue in the county has more than eight courts; the next largest is Lauren C. Bolles, with eight lined courts.

One: Manzano Mesa Pickleball Complex, where twenty-one of thirty-three courts are stated lit. No other published venue carries a lighting answer. The City's other two lighting statements, eight lit courts at Alamosa Park and twelve at Ventana Ranch Park, belong to venues whose addresses cannot be resolved.

sources.evidence: The City's pickleball page, whose "Pickleball Court Locations" table states a name, an address and a description cell for sixteen venues, thirteen of which publish: "Manzano Mesa Pickleball Complex / 501 Elizabeth SE / Pickleball Complex / 33 Courts (21 Lighted)", "Villela Pickleball Courts / 4800 Cherokee NE / Pickleball Complex / 6 Courts", "Sierra Vista Tennis Complex / 5001 Montano Rd. NW / Tennis/Pickleball Courts / 2 Courts and 4 Lined Courts", nine parks labelled "Tennis Courts with Pickleball Lines" (Hoffman 2, Rinconada 2, Montgomery 6, Columbus 4, Eagle Ranch 4, Loma Del Norte 4, Lynnewood 4, Lauren C. Bolles 8, Quintessence 4) and "Wells Park / 500 Mountain NW / 3 Pickleball Courts" with no kind stated. The refused rows: "Pat Hurley Park / 3828 Rincon Rd NW / 4 Courts and 4 Lined Courts", "Alamosa Park / 1100 Bataan SW / 8 Lighted Pickleball Courts", "Ventana Ranch Park / 10000 Universe NW / 12 Lighted Pickleball Courts". Prose: "The City of Albuquerque has two dedicated pickleball complexes: Manzano Mesa Pickleball Complex, and Villella Pickleball Courts." "Manzano Mesa, Villella, and Pat Hurley are open from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily." "Courts are typically available on a first come, first serve basis and play is limited to 1.5 hours when others are waiting." "Pickleball lessons for juniors and adults will take place at Manzano Mesa Pickleball Complex." The page source holds two older tables inside an HTML comment, not rendered by a browser, naming Barelas Park, Los Altos Park and Zuni Park and giving different counts at Manzano Mesa, Eagle Ranch, Montgomery and Ventana Ranch. Snapshot: data/sources/albuquerque/pickleball.html
sources.not_stated: Anything about any other municipality in Bernalillo County, the County's own parks, price, surface, parking, indoor or outdoor, or lighting at any published venue but Manzano Mesa.

sources.evidence: All thirteen published addresses matched at house-number level through the Census address file and were placed in Bernalillo County, NM (FIPS 35001), inside the incorporated place "Albuquerque city"; the City writes most addresses without a street type and the Census supplied one, and no second resolver was needed. Seven published addresses carry the City's NE quadrant, five NW and one SE. "3828 Rincon Rd NW" (Pat Hurley Park), "1100 Bataan SW" (Alamosa Park) and "10000 Universe NW" (Ventana Ranch Park) are found by neither the Census address file nor OpenStreetMap.
